e-4505.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product
e-4505.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8\end{aligned}
$$
e-4505.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. The variable $y$ does not appear in the first equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ So, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+0y=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/cdadd8a9c68f58c4d8434e658d4acffeba524850f361fcd3d6fe3524b3d781a1.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/35104266eb5a086bef0536640ec1310532cc136a251049a1adcfe4418ef0ef89.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/aa4de061ca95088763e7e5fec289dbd2e5bd298e8986ef6660617ea0ba227821.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/10781c0f9183c793e3f2de287ede937e764d942767ecc9b64942dc338c1e1307.png)

e-4506.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product by Reorganizing
e-4506.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-5y=-3x \\ 6+x=-2+y\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
e-4506.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3x-5y=0 \\ x-y=-8.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/648952bc6e093c08ff29215fce21fe115ab81e9fc3d8b423772123eae31237f3.png)

is the coefficient matrix,

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/c1f203be0770c298d9c2c75ccfbfb30354cb314ed75c8b05f6639e5633ca7442.png)

is the column vector of constants, and

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/aa4de061ca95088763e7e5fec289dbd2e5bd298e8986ef6660617ea0ba227821.png)

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/75aed8c54a2ec274def967802cbd3b67d0fad3358e676b02cf52e1e8d2cbe0d7.png)

e-4507.knowledge_point: Expressing a Matrix Product as a 2x2 System of Equations
e-4507.problem:
What is the system of equations represented by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052302/assets/6f0ddb43928e0d9f52ca2fe0f0ab578adfa986cba8179746bd34a50a1a7c506b.png)
e-4507.worked_solution:
The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10x-15y=5 \\ 1x+0y=-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=1 \\ x=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Represent the following system of equations using matrices: {2x−y=7x+y=−3

a

b
[1211][xy]=[37]
c
[1−121][xy]=[73]
d
[2111][xy]=[−37]
e
[2−111][xy]=[7−3]
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficient rows are (2, -1) and (1, 1), and the corresponding constants are 7 and -3. Thus option e reproduces both equations.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=7 \\ x+y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation, all the variables are on the left-hand side, and all the constants are on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=7 \\ x+y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product
content.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=7 \\ x+y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation, all the variables are on the left-hand side, and all the constants are on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-y=7 \\ x+y=-3\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Represent the following system of equations using matrices: {2x+y=4x−y=−10

a
[−2111][xy]=[4−1]
b
[21−1−1][xy]=[−41]
c
[121−1][xy]=[−41]
d
[211−1][xy]=[4−10]
e
[121−1][xy]=[410]
Submit

decision.explanation: The coefficient rows are (2, 1) and (1, -1), with constants 4 and -10. Multiplying the matrix in option d by the variables vector reproduces both equations.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+y=4 \\ x-y=-10\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation, all the variables are on the left-hand side, and all the constants are on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+y=4 \\ x-y=-10\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product
content.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+y=4 \\ x-y=-10\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation, all the variables are on the left-hand side, and all the constants are on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+y=4 \\ x-y=-10\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -10\end{aligned}].
$$

First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. The variable $y$ does not appear in the first equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ Similarly, the variable $x$ does not appear in the second equation, which means that its coefficient is $0$ too. 

So, we get

$$
{\begin{aligned}-5x+0y=10 \\ 0x+4y=-12\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -12\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -12\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: The coefficient rows are (-2,5) and (5,0), since the second equation has no y term. The corresponding constants are -1 and 15, giving option d.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. 
The variable $y$ does not appear in the second equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x+0y=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product
content.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. 
The variable $y$ does not appear in the second equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-2x+5y=-1 \\ 5x+0y=15\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 15\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 8
?

Represent the following system of equations using matrices: {x=y−1x=−y+1

a
[1−111][xy]=[00]
b
[1111][xy]=[01]
c
[1−111][xy]=[−11]
d
[1−111][xy]=[11]
e
[1−111][xy]=[0−1]
Submit

decision.explanation: Rearranging gives x-y=-1 and x+y=1. Their coefficient rows are (1,-1) and (1,1), with constants -1 and 1, matching option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x=y-1 \\ x=-y+1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and  both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y=-1 \\ x+y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Representing a 2x2 System of Equations Using a Matrix Product by Reorganizing
content.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x=y-1 \\ x=-y+1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and  both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y=-1 \\ x+y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}16 \\ -18\end{aligned}]?
$$

after.worked_solution:
The $2\times 2$ matrix encodes the coefficients of $x$ and $y$, and the $2\times 1$ vector on the right gives the constants, so the system is

$$
{\begin{aligned}8x-4y=16 \\ -6x+12y=-18\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the first equation by $4$ and the second by $-6$ gives the simplified system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y=4 \\ x-2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

which matches the entries shown above.

before.html:
Question 12
?

What is the system of equations represented by [0−1−312][xy]=[0−15]?

a
{y=0−4x+y=5
b
{y=5x−4y=0
c
{y=0x−4y=5
d
{x=0x−4y=5
e
{x=0x−3y=5
Submit

decision.explanation: Matrix multiplication gives -y=0 and -3x+12y=-15. These simplify to y=0 and x-4y=5, matching option c.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem:
What is the system of equations represented by

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -15\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-y=0 \\ -3x+12y=-15.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y=0 \\ x-4y=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 12
?

What is the system of equations represented by [0−1−312][xy]=[0−15]?

a
{y=0−4x+y=5
b
{y=5x−4y=0
c
{y=0x−4y=5
d
{x=0x−4y=5
e
{x=0x−3y=5
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The 2×2 matrix represents the coefficients of x and y, while the 2×1 column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

{0x−y=0−3x+12y=−15.

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

{y=0x−4y=5.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms -y=0 and -3x+12y=-15, which simplify to y=0 and x-4y=5. This is option c; the deliberately submitted option d incorrectly states x=0.

content.knowledge_point: Expressing a Matrix Product as a 2x2 System of Equations
content.problem:
What is the system of equations represented by

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -15\end{aligned}]?
$$
content.worked_solution:
The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}0x-y=0 \\ -3x+12y=-15.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y=0 \\ x-4y=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 13
?

What is the system of equations represented by [1025123][xy]=[15−6]?

a
{2x+5y=154x+y=−6
b
{10x+25y=−1512x+3y=6
c
{10x+5y=−1512x+3y=6
d
{2x+5y=34x+y=−2
e
{10x+25y=−1512x+6y=3
Submit

decision.explanation: Matrix multiplication gives 10x+25y=15 and 12x+3y=-6. Dividing the first equation by 5 and the second by 3 gives 2x+5y=3 and 4x+y=-2, matching option d.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem:
What is the system of equations represented by

$$
[\begin{aligned}10 & 25 \\ 12 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}15 \\ -6\end{aligned}]?
$$
after.worked_solution:
The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10x+25y=15 \\ 12x+3y=-6\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x+5y=3 \\ 4x+y=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}10x+25y=15 \\ 12x+3y=-6\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
